description: 10 realistic customer complaints for testing the complaint resolution assistant. Some contain hidden legal significance that a well-built tool should detect.

complaints.subject: Invoice query — February 2026
complaints.message: Hi, I just received invoice INV-2026-0892 for EUR 3,850. This doesn't match what we agreed. Our Order Form says EUR 3,000 per month. Can you explain the difference? Thanks, Markus

agent_actions: Pull invoice INV-2026-0892 and compare to Order Form
Check if EUR 850 difference matches any add-on or overage charge
If billing error: issue credit note (within agent authority at EUR 850)
If correct: explain with Order Form reference

complaints.subject: Platform outage — production system affected
complaints.message: Your platform was completely unavailable from 14:30 to 19:15 yesterday (February 11). This is 4 hours and 45 minutes of downtime. Our production scheduling system runs on your platform and we had to halt a production line. I need to know what happened, when it will be fixed for good, and what credits we are entitled to under our SLA. This is unacceptable.

agent_actions: Acknowledge within SLA — do not dispute downtime claim
Pull infrastructure incident log for Feb 11, 14:30–19:15
Calculate SLA credit: 4h45m downtime on 99.5% SLA (threshold = ~3.6h/month) — credits apply
Credit = 5% of monthly fee per 0.5% below SLA. Monthly fee = EUR 10,000. Calculate and confirm
Enterprise customer — escalate to Account Manager Thomas Weber
Prepare Root Cause Analysis within 5 business days
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: Enterprise customer with large contract. If SLA breach persists, termination right may be triggered. Account Manager must be looped in.

complaints.subject: Please delete all our data
complaints.message: Hello, we have decided to move to a different provider. I would like you to delete all data we have stored on your system, including all user accounts, documents, and logs. Please confirm when this has been done. Also, one of my employees, Anna Nowak, would like to know what personal data you hold about her specifically. Kind regards, Jan Kowalski

agent_actions: IMMEDIATELY log receipt date — 1-month GDPR clock starts today (2026-02-14)
Identify TWO separate DSR types: (1) erasure request (Art. 17) from company, (2) access request (Art. 15) from Anna Nowak
Route to DPO within 4 hours
Acknowledge receipt to customer within 24 hours
Note: erasure may conflict with contract data retention obligations — DPO to assess
Verify identity of Anna Nowak before processing her individual request (separate from company request)
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: This appears to be a simple cancellation but contains TWO GDPR DSRs buried in the message: (1) a company data erasure request and (2) an individual access request (Art. 15) from a named employee. A naive agent might treat this as just a cancellation. The GDPR obligations have strict deadlines.

complaints.subject: Cancellation
complaints.message: Hi, I want to cancel my subscription. We're not happy with the product. Please confirm cancellation. Sandra

agent_actions: Pull the contract to determine: initial term, auto-renewal status, notice period
Classify cancellation type: convenience (no specific reason given)
Calculate: 90-day notice period starts from date of this email (2026-02-15), last day of service = 2026-05-16
Confirm: prepaid fees are non-refundable
Offer save conversation (customer is not invoking a legal right — save attempt is appropriate)
Loop in Account Manager Lena Fischer for save attempt
Acknowledge cancellation in writing to start the notice clock
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: Simple convenience cancellation. However, the notice period must be acknowledged in writing as this starts the contractual clock. Do not ignore this step.

customer.name: Rechtsanwältin Claudia Bergmann
customer.company: Kanzlei Bergmann & Söhne (acting for: TechCorp Solutions GmbH)

complaints.subject: Formal Notice of Material Breach — Contract No. TC-2024-0043
complaints.message: We act on behalf of TechCorp Solutions GmbH in relation to Contract No. TC-2024-0043 dated 1 March 2024. We hereby formally notify TechForward Solutions GmbH of a material breach of the above agreement arising from the repeated failure to meet the uptime SLA commitments set out in Section 5.1. Our client has experienced five separate outages exceeding the monthly SLA threshold in the period October 2025 to January 2026. Pursuant to Section 4.3 of the contract, our client is entitled to terminate for cause and to seek damages for losses incurred as a result of the service failures. Our client intends to exercise the termination right unless TechForward provides a formal remediation plan with binding commitments within 14 days of this notice. All further correspondence should be directed to this office. Claudia Bergmann, Rechtsanwältin

agent_actions: DO NOT send any substantive response
Send Template 10A (receipt acknowledgment only) within 2 hours
Forward immediately to Legal team lead and Account Manager Thomas Weber
Log receipt timestamp — 14-day response deadline starts today (2026-02-17), deadline = 2026-03-03
Preserve all records related to TC-2024-0043 and the five cited outages
Do NOT contact the customer directly — all correspondence goes through the law firm
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: This is a formal legal notice from a lawyer. The 14-day remediation deadline is contractually significant. If TechForward does not respond by 2026-03-03, the customer may be entitled to terminate immediately. This is extremely time-sensitive and must reach Legal within hours, not days.

complaints.subject: Login not working since yesterday
complaints.message: My login stopped working yesterday afternoon around 3pm. I've tried resetting my password three times but I still can't get in. The reset email isn't arriving either. I've got a board presentation in 2 hours that needs data from the platform. Please fix this urgently.

agent_actions: Treat as URGENT due to 2-hour deadline — escalate to technical support immediately
Verify identity before making account changes
Check: (1) is account active in admin console, (2) is email system delivering reset emails, (3) is account flagged for any reason
If technical issue: engage on-call engineer immediately
Provide interim workaround if possible (e.g., read-only link, temporary access)
Follow up to confirm access is restored before the presentation
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: Time-critical due to the 2-hour presentation deadline. Standard SLA (4 hours first response) would be too slow. Agent should treat this as a P1 urgency situation and escalate engineering immediately.

complaints.subject: Strange emails — possible security issue
complaints.message: Hi, I want to flag something odd. Several of my employees have received emails this morning that look like they come from TechForward but have a slightly different sender domain (techf0rward.com instead of techforward.com). The emails are asking them to log in and verify their credentials. None of my staff clicked the links. Could this be a phishing attack using our data somehow? Has there been any kind of breach on your end? Very concerned.

agent_actions: Escalate to SIRT IMMEDIATELY — within 15 minutes
Send Template 5A only — no other response, no speculation
Log exact timestamp: 2026-02-19 [time received] — potential 72-hour GDPR clock may start now
Do NOT confirm or deny whether a breach occurred
Do NOT investigate independently
SIRT to determine: (a) is techf0rward.com domain related to TechForward systems, (b) is customer data involved in a potential exfiltration, (c) GDPR notification obligation assessment
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: A customer-facing phishing campaign using a lookalike domain may indicate that customer email data was exposed in a breach. Even if TechForward systems are not compromised, the GDPR clock may start from when the customer reports this to TechForward. Time-critical escalation required.

complaints.subject: Refund — I signed up by mistake
complaints.message: Hi, I signed up for your platform on February 18th but this was a mistake — my colleague was supposed to sign up but used my account and payment details. I haven't used the platform at all. I would like a full refund please. Thanks, Patrick

agent_actions: Check contract signature date: February 18, 2026
Check today's date: February 20, 2026 — 2 days since signing
Assess cooling-off eligibility: B2B contracts — check if contractual cooling-off applies (some TechForward B2B contracts include a 14-day cooling-off clause)
If cooling-off applies: process full refund, cancel subscription, Template 3B
If no contractual cooling-off and customer has not activated the service: consider goodwill refund (within agent authority up to EUR 200; above that requires Finance)
Annual contract value = EUR 14,400; monthly = EUR 1,200 — above agent authority for full refund
Escalate to Finance for approval if full refund needed
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: Customer signed 2 days ago and hasn't used the platform. A 14-day cooling-off period may apply depending on the contract type. Even if not contractually required, a goodwill approach may be appropriate for a basic tier customer who hasn't activated. Agent cannot approve full refund without Finance sign-off.

complaints.subject: Your employee was very rude
complaints.message: I want to make a formal complaint. I had a support call this morning with someone called 'Jonas' and he was extremely rude and dismissive. When I explained my issue he told me I was 'probably doing it wrong' and hung up on me before I finished explaining. I have been a customer for 3 years and have never been treated like this. I expect an apology and I want to make sure this doesn't happen again. Maria

agent_actions: Acknowledge with genuine empathy — do not minimize or defend
Do NOT name, identify, or make any statement about 'Jonas'
Do NOT investigate or promise a specific disciplinary outcome
Route to Customer Care Manager and HR within 4 hours
Ensure Jonas does not contact this customer pending review
Confirm to Maria that her complaint has been registered and the appropriate team will follow up within 3 business days
Note: Maria is a 3-year customer — high retention risk. Ensure Account Manager Sarah Klein is also informed
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: Long-standing customer with high retention value. The complaint has HR and employment law implications — cannot be handled by an agent. The agent's role is to acknowledge and route, not investigate. Risk of losing a loyal customer if handled poorly.

complaints.subject: We are very unhappy
complaints.message: Hello. We have been using TechForward for about 8 months now and to be honest we are not very happy with it. The platform works most of the time but there have been a few crashes, the interface is confusing, the reporting module doesn't do what we need, and the onboarding wasn't great. We expected more. We're not sure if we want to continue after the contract ends. What can you do for us? Klaus

agent_actions: Read carefully for any hidden specific complaint — note: 'a few crashes' may be a CAT-07 (bug) or CAT-02 (SLA) issue worth investigating separately
Acknowledge the overall frustration genuinely
Ask one clarifying question: which of the issues is causing the most day-to-day impact?
Offer to arrange a review call with Account Manager Sarah Klein to address the reporting module gap
Log feedback themes in CRM: (1) UI/UX confusion, (2) reporting capability gap, (3) onboarding quality — valuable for product team
Assess retention risk: customer is 8 months in, contract may renew in 4 months — flag to Account Manager
expected_classification.hidden_complexity: Vague on the surface but contains at least 3 distinct issues: (1) 'a few crashes' — potential SLA claim worth investigating; (2) reporting module gap — potential product feedback or custom requirement; (3) onboarding complaint — potential warranty/SOW issue. The agent must read carefully and may need to re-classify part of this complaint.
